title: Informed Consent Deficiencies in FDA Clinical Investigator Form 483s and Warning Letters Under 21 CFR Part 50
summary: The informed consent deficiencies recurring in FDA clinical investigator warning letters, with Form 483 examples, mapped to the requirements of 21 CFR Part 50.
body_markdown:
## Informed consent deficiencies in FDA clinical investigator warning letters and Form 483s, and what 21 CFR Part 50 requires


### Key findings


FDA's Bioresearch Monitoring (BIMO) enforcement record shows that informed consent findings are rarely about a missing signature alone. The recurring problems are process failures. Sites consent with the wrong document, consent after research procedures have started, enroll without legally effective consent from the right person, or use consent forms that leave out required elements or contain prohibited language.


The pattern below comes from 154 FDA warning letters issued from 2005 to 2026 to clinical investigators, sponsor-investigators and bioavailability/bioequivalence (BA/BE) clinical sites whose text addresses informed consent. Of these, 130 cite at least one informed consent deficiency. The counts show how many letters contain each type of finding (one letter can contain several). They describe this set of letters, not an official FDA statistic. Form 483 examples cited below are illustrations and are not part of the 154-letter count.


Deficiency category Letters citing it Representative findings


Consent form not IRB-approved, or an outdated or superseded version used 51 38 of 56 subjects signed forms the IRB had never reviewed[395](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603212406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075960.htm)[393](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603212406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075960.htm) . 7 of 16 subjects signed a superseded screening ICF after a newer version was approved[1044](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm148993.htm)[1043](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm148993.htm) .


Consent obtained after study procedures began 37 Subjects were randomized days to months before signing[382](https://web.archive.org/web/20190214032318/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2013/ucm340269.htm)[376](https://web.archive.org/web/20190214032318/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2013/ucm340269.htm) . Screening and placebo run-in started about 14 days before consent[459](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/mobeen-mazhar-md-660335-05312023)[460](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/mobeen-mazhar-md-660335-05312023) .


Missing or improper signatures and dates 32 Study staff, not the signers, dated the consent documents[438](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm)[431](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm)[277](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630073833/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048200.htm)[271](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630073833/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048200.htm) . Signed consent documents were missing for enrolled subjects[415](https://web.archive.org/web/20151004052012/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm152450.htm)[417](https://web.archive.org/web/20151004052012/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm152450.htm) .


Required 50.25 elements missing, or exculpatory language 31 Exculpatory release-of-liability language[521](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/kdunn-and-associates-pa-dba-healthquilt-611864-02162021)[517](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/kdunn-and-associates-pa-dba-healthquilt-611864-02162021)[233](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423062211/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2014/ucm393082.htm)[230](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423062211/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2014/ucm393082.htm) . Risks and experimental procedures were not described[1020](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/maggie-jeffries-md-avanti-anesthesiology-llc-646498-03032023)[1015](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/maggie-jeffries-md-avanti-anesthesiology-llc-646498-03032023) .


No consent obtained at all (including for optional procedures) 22 Subjects were screened and randomized without ever consenting[325](https://web.archive.org/web/20160318215253/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2007/ucm076521.htm)[326](https://web.archive.org/web/20160318215253/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2007/ucm076521.htm) . Optional samples were collected without the separate consent required[507](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/shirish-m-gadgeel-md-716181-09042025)[505](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/shirish-m-gadgeel-md-716181-09042025)[476](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/mark-s-dacey-md-722942-02022026)[474](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/mark-s-dacey-md-722942-02022026) .


LAR, pediatric permission, language or short-form problems 14 Pediatric subjects were enrolled on the signature of a sibling or uncle[312](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/americo-f-padilla-md-700447-03252025)[315](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/americo-f-padilla-md-700447-03252025) . Non-English speakers signed English documents with no translated short form[437](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm)[431](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm) .


Failure to re-consent after new risk information 14 Ongoing subjects were not re-consented with IRB-approved revisions that added new risks[452](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015144139/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm131662.htm)[453](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015144139/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm131662.htm)[449](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015144139/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm131662.htm) .


Falsified or altered consent records 9 Fabricated LAR signatures[434](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm)[428](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm) . Investigator signatures cut and pasted onto consent documents[322](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423060542/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2015/ucm540515.htm)[318](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423060542/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2015/ucm540515.htm) .


Copy of the consent form not given to the subject 4 Copies were given only on request[1019](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/maggie-jeffries-md-avanti-anesthesiology-llc-646498-03032023)[1015](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/maggie-jeffries-md-avanti-anesthesiology-llc-646498-03032023)[255](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015142604/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075302.htm)[250](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015142604/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075302.htm) .


Other (assent, emergency exception, opportunity to consider, undue influence) 36 Child assent not obtained[985](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603195755/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075845.htm)[989](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603195755/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075845.htm) . Emergency-exception certification and 5-working-day reporting failures[243](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603195544/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075789.htm)[237](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603195544/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075789.htm)[488](https://web.archive.org/web/20150613094401/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048424.htm)[489](https://web.archive.org/web/20150613094401/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048424.htm) .


The provisions these letters cite include 21 CFR 50.20, 21 CFR 812.100 for device investigators, 21 CFR 50.27(a), and 21 CFR 312.60 for drug and biologic investigators. Letters also cite specific 50.25(a) elements, the short-form provision at 50.27(b)(2), and 50.55 for child assent[431](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm)[436](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm) .


### The most frequently cited deficiencies


#### 1. Unapproved or outdated consent documents


This is the most common finding. Section 50.27(a) requires a written consent form "approved by the IRB"[440](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.27) , so using any other version breaks the documentation requirement even when the subject did sign. Typical patterns:


- **Forms that were never IRB-approved.** In one device study, at least 38 of 56 enrolled subjects signed forms that had not been reviewed and approved by the IRB, and those forms also lacked required contact information[395](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603212406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075960.htm)[396](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603212406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075960.htm)[397](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603212406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075960.htm) . Other letters cite general surgical consent forms used instead of the study ICF[268](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603182642/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2007/ucm076381.htm)[270](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603182642/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2007/ucm076381.htm) , and forms that were neither study-specific nor IRB-approved[770](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/john-meadors-559611-10152018)[772](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/john-meadors-559611-10152018)[745](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/richard-j-obiso-phd-dba-avila-herbals-llc-622821-02042022) .
- **Superseded versions.** Seven of sixteen subjects signed an outdated screening ICF after the IRB had approved a newer version[1044](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm148993.htm) . In another case, subjects signed versions that were several years old and so did not get updated outcome and safety data[286](https://web.archive.org/web/20150920231121/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm197438.htm)[287](https://web.archive.org/web/20150920231121/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm197438.htm)[288](https://web.archive.org/web/20150920231121/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm197438.htm) .
- **Altering an approved form.** A December 2025 Form 483 cites a study coordinator who changed the procedure section of the IRB-approved consent while reviewing it with subjects, which left the form used no longer IRB-approved[1073](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/informed-consent-deficiencies-in-fda-clinical?showSourceNumber=1073)[1072](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/informed-consent-deficiencies-in-fda-clinical?showSourceNumber=1072) .
- **Consent signed under an expired approval.** One letter cites a subject who was consented and received the investigational device after IRB approval had expired[931](https://web.archive.org/web/20150921000137/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm175774.htm)[929](https://web.archive.org/web/20150921000137/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm175774.htm) .


#### 2. Consent obtained after research procedures began


Section 50.20 requires legally effective consent before the person is involved as a research subject[427](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.20) . FDA consistently treats research-only screening tests, randomization, run-in dosing and protocol blood draws as involvement:


- Subjects were randomized more than three weeks, four days and more than two months before signing the procedure consent. A research-specific CT angiogram was done the day before screening consent[379](https://web.archive.org/web/20190214032318/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2013/ucm340269.htm)[380](https://web.archive.org/web/20190214032318/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2013/ucm340269.htm)[382](https://web.archive.org/web/20190214032318/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2013/ucm340269.htm) .
- Four of 23 subjects had protocol baseline blood drawn before they signed. FDA rejected the investigator's explanation that verbal consent came first[343](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630073807/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048320.htm)[344](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630073807/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048320.htm)[345](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630073807/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048320.htm) .
- All subjects in one study were screened, randomized and given case numbers before consenting[325](https://web.archive.org/web/20160318215253/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2007/ucm076521.htm)[326](https://web.archive.org/web/20160318215253/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2007/ucm076521.htm) .
- A 2026 letter cites pregnancy testing, vital signs and blood collection before parental consent, and screening recorded as complete before consent, with no applicable exception[702](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/adnan-dahdul-md-719607-03122026)[701](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/adnan-dahdul-md-719607-03122026) .
- BA/BE clinical sites draw similar observations. One 2026 Form 483 cites 48 enrolled subjects (plus additional subjects) who had mammograms, transvaginal ultrasounds, Pap smears and estradiol testing under a general screening consent before study-specific consent[1067](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/informed-consent-deficiencies-in-fda-clinical?showSourceNumber=1067) . An earlier 483 cites study-specific screening tests done without prior consent, under a screening consent that also omitted risks, alternatives, contacts and voluntariness[1056](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/informed-consent-deficiencies-in-fda-clinical?showSourceNumber=1056) .


#### 3. Signature and date defects


Section 50.27(a) requires the form to be signed and dated by the subject or LAR at the time of consent[440](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.27) . Letters cite:


- Investigators or coordinators, rather than the subjects, dating subjects' signatures[277](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630073833/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048200.htm)[271](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630073833/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048200.htm)[737](https://web.archive.org/web/20151013113136/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075434.htm)[738](https://web.archive.org/web/20151013113136/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075434.htm) . In one case the investigator acknowledged routinely inserting dates before parents signed[438](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm)[431](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm) .
- Missing subject or LAR signatures on consent documents, including visit-specific consents[415](https://web.archive.org/web/20151004052012/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm152450.htm)[417](https://web.archive.org/web/20151004052012/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm152450.htm)[418](https://web.archive.org/web/20151004052012/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm152450.htm) .
- A subject with no signature agreeing to genetic testing whose records nonetheless held genetic results from a later buccal sample[782](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/namita-goyal-md-677324-10102024)[784](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/namita-goyal-md-677324-10102024) .
- Investigator signatures dated before the subject's signature, white-out over dates, and consent times that could not be checked against procedure times. FDA treats these as documentation failures even where it does not allege backdating[895](https://web.archive.org/web/20151013113136/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075445.htm)[900](https://web.archive.org/web/20151013113136/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075445.htm)[890](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603195544/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075797.htm)[344](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630073807/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048320.htm)[757](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/ignatius-p-godoy-md-561662-10012018)[759](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/ignatius-p-godoy-md-561662-10012018) .


#### 4. Consent forms missing required elements or containing exculpatory language


Letters regularly line up consent document content against 50.25 and the exculpatory-language ban in 50.20:


- **Exculpatory language.** Forms that required subjects to waive claims or release the investigator and others from liability[521](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/kdunn-and-associates-pa-dba-healthquilt-611864-02162021)[517](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/kdunn-and-associates-pa-dba-healthquilt-611864-02162021)[233](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423062211/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2014/ucm393082.htm)[230](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423062211/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2014/ucm393082.htm)[296](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015142604/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075286.htm) .
- **Missing basic elements.** Omitted foreseeable risks, alternatives and benefits[253](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015142604/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075302.htm)[297](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015142604/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075286.htm)[298](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015142604/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075286.htm)[300](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015142604/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075286.htm) . No statement that participation is research and voluntary[234](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423062211/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2014/ucm393082.htm) . No statement that FDA may inspect records[247](https://web.archive.org/web/20150613121257/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048268.htm)[248](https://web.archive.org/web/20150613121257/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048268.htm) . No contacts for questions, subjects' rights and research injury[299](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015142604/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075286.htm)[397](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603212406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075960.htm) .
- **Statements that misdescribe the study.** A form saying no part of the study was experimental[542](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/pratik-doshi-md-alembic-pharmaceuticals-ltd-731020-07102026)[545](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/pratik-doshi-md-alembic-pharmaceuticals-ltd-731020-07102026)[546](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/pratik-doshi-md-alembic-pharmaceuticals-ltd-731020-07102026) . Forms stating there were no additional study-related risks[1020](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/maggie-jeffries-md-avanti-anesthesiology-llc-646498-03032023) . A placebo described in a study that used no placebo[246](https://web.archive.org/web/20150613121257/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048268.htm) . Forms claiming or implying FDA authorization or marketing clearance[473](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603212406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075951.htm)[552](https://web.archive.org/web/20150613115712/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048352.htm) . BA/BE consent forms that attributed approval and effectiveness to both test and reference products and overstated benefits[483](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/sourav-k-mishra-md-all-india-institute-medical-sciences-724881-04292026)[484](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/sourav-k-mishra-md-all-india-institute-medical-sciences-724881-04292026)[640](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/mukesh-b-chandre-md-mbbsashirwad-hospital-research-centre-724911-04292026) .
- **Cost disclosure.** A Form 483 cites a consent document that did not disclose additional research-related costs set out in a separately signed billing agreement[1076](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/informed-consent-deficiencies-in-fda-clinical?showSourceNumber=1076)[1077](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/informed-consent-deficiencies-in-fda-clinical?showSourceNumber=1077) .


#### 5. No legally effective consent at all


The most serious findings involve enrolling or treating subjects with no consent. Examples:


- A 2019 Form 483 cites two studies involving 747 and at least 874 subjects enrolled and treated without legally effective consent, neither meeting the 50.23 or 50.24 exceptions[1070](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/informed-consent-deficiencies-in-fda-clinical?showSourceNumber=1070) .
- Children were randomized with no consent on file after their parents had reportedly refused participation[753](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/ignatius-p-godoy-md-561662-10012018)[755](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/ignatius-p-godoy-md-561662-10012018) .
- Recent letters often involve **optional or add-on components** : optional genetic samples collected without the separate consent[507](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/shirish-m-gadgeel-md-716181-09042025)[505](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/shirish-m-gadgeel-md-716181-09042025) , an optional aqueous humor collection done after the subject had twice declined it[476](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/mark-s-dacey-md-722942-02022026)[474](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/mark-s-dacey-md-722942-02022026) , study-drug consent addenda never signed[501](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/mark-j-savant-mdsan-francisco-research-institute-712306-06262025)[502](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/mark-j-savant-mdsan-francisco-research-institute-712306-06262025) , and optional pharmacokinetic sampling without the optional consent[435](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm)[431](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm) .


#### 6. Who is consenting: LARs, parents, language and witnesses


Section 50.3 defines a legally authorized representative as a person or body "authorized under applicable law" to consent for the subject, and defines parental "permission" and "guardian" separately[348](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.3)[350](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.3)[351](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.3) . Letters cite:


- Pediatric subjects enrolled on the signature of a sibling and an uncle, with real parental permission obtained 9 to 10 months later[312](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/americo-f-padilla-md-700447-03252025)[315](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/americo-f-padilla-md-700447-03252025)[310](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/americo-f-padilla-md-700447-03252025) .
- A child in state custody enrolled with only a parent's signature, when the state agency was the only authorized representative[339](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604112833/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2010/ucm202614.htm)[340](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604112833/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2010/ucm202614.htm) .
- Someone signing for a subject without documentation that they were the LAR[257](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604131009/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2011/ucm244485.htm)[260](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604131009/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2011/ucm244485.htm) , and others signing where the IRB-approved process allowed only the subject to sign[783](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/namita-goyal-md-677324-10102024) .
- Non-English-speaking subjects or representatives signing English-language documents with no translated form or short form[437](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm)[247](https://web.archive.org/web/20150613121257/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048268.htm)[249](https://web.archive.org/web/20150613121257/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048268.htm)[462](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604153912/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2011/ucm248222.htm)[464](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604153912/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2011/ucm248222.htm) .
- Witnesses whose impartiality was not documented[783](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/namita-goyal-md-677324-10102024) , and witness signatures that could not be verified[711](https://web.archive.org/web/20151013123232/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075592.htm)[713](https://web.archive.org/web/20151013123232/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075592.htm) .


#### 7. Re-consent and new information


When the IRB approves a revised consent carrying new risk information, failing to re-consent ongoing subjects is cited as a Part 50 violation. In one oncology letter, the site did not re-consent 6, 9 and 1 ongoing subjects under three successive revisions that added risks such as serious confusion, thromboembolic events and fatal lung injury[450](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015144139/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm131662.htm)[452](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015144139/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm131662.htm)[453](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015144139/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm131662.htm)[454](https://web.archive.org/web/20151015144139/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm131662.htm) . Other letters cite telephone or mail re-consent processes that the IRB had not approved or that were not documented[883](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604132907/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2011/ucm268290.htm)[884](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604132907/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2011/ucm268290.htm)[389](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603191753/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2007/ucm076383.htm) .


#### 8. Integrity of the consent record


A smaller but serious group of letters involves fabricated LAR signatures[434](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm)[428](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm) , investigator signatures cut and pasted onto consent documents[322](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423060542/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2015/ucm540515.htm)[318](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423060542/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2015/ucm540515.htm) , signature times changed so consent appeared to precede vaccination[757](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/ignatius-p-godoy-md-561662-10012018)[758](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/ignatius-p-godoy-md-561662-10012018) , and original consent forms destroyed or lost[831](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603224505/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm076082.htm)[828](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603224505/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm076082.htm) .


### What 21 CFR Part 50 requires


#### General requirements (21 CFR 50.20)


Except as provided in 50.22, 50.23 and 50.24, no investigator may involve a human being as a research subject without first obtaining "legally effective informed consent" from the subject or the subject's legally authorized representative[427](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.20) . Consent must be sought only under circumstances that:


- give "sufficient opportunity to consider whether or not to participate"[427](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.20) , and
- minimize "the possibility of coercion or undue influence"[427](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.20) .


The information given to the subject or the representative must be "in language understandable to the subject or the representative"[427](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.20) .


No oral or written consent may include exculpatory language through which the subject waives or appears to waive legal rights, or releases or appears to release the investigator, sponsor, institution or its agents from liability for negligence[427](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.20) . FDA has used the "opportunity to consider" standard in findings where recorded intervals between arrival and procedure left too little time to read the consent document[841](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006222021/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm148352.htm)[842](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006222021/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm148352.htm) , and where a subject got the form after their eyes had been dilated[707](https://web.archive.org/web/20190214031437/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2013/ucm360128.htm) .


#### Elements of informed consent (21 CFR 50.25)


**Basic elements (50.25(a)).** Each subject must receive[356](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25) :


1. A statement that the study involves research, its purposes, expected duration, procedures, and identification of any experimental procedures[357](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25)
2. Reasonably foreseeable risks or discomforts[358](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25)
3. Reasonably expected benefits to the subject or others[359](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25)
4. Appropriate alternative procedures or courses of treatment[360](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25)
5. The extent of confidentiality of records, noting that FDA may inspect them[361](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25)
6. For more-than-minimal-risk research, whether compensation and medical treatment are available for injury[362](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25)
7. Whom to contact about the research, subjects' rights and research-related injury[363](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25)
8. That participation is voluntary, refusal involves no penalty or loss of benefits, and the subject may stop at any time[364](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25)


**Additional elements (50.25(b)), when appropriate**[365](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25) : unforeseeable risks, including to an embryo or fetus[366](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25) ; circumstances under which the investigator may end participation[367](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25) ; additional costs[368](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25) ; consequences of withdrawal[369](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25) ; that significant new findings will be provided[370](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25) ; and the approximate number of subjects[371](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25) .


**ClinicalTrials.gov statement (50.25(c)).** For applicable clinical trials, the consent documents and process must include the prescribed statement that a description of the trial will be available on ClinicalTrials.gov[372](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.25) .


#### Documentation (21 CFR 50.27)


- **General rule (50.27(a)).** Except as provided in 56.109(c), consent must be documented with a written consent form approved by the IRB, signed and dated at the time of consent by the subject or LAR. A copy must be given to the person signing[440](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.27) .
- **Long form (50.27(b)(1)).** The document must include the 50.25 elements. It may be read aloud, but the subject or LAR must have adequate opportunity to read it before signing[441](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.27) .
- **Short form (50.27(b)(2)).** The 50.25 elements are presented orally with a witness present, using an IRB-approved written summary. The subject or LAR signs the short form. The witness signs both the short form and the summary. The person obtaining consent signs the summary. The subject or LAR gets copies of both[442](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.27) .


#### Emergency exception (21 CFR 50.23)


Use of a test article without consent requires that, before use, the investigator and a physician not otherwise participating in the investigation certify in writing that[331](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.23) : the subject faces a life-threatening situation[332](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.23) ; consent cannot be obtained from the subject[333](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.23) ; there is not enough time to obtain consent from the legal representative[334](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.23) ; and no alternative approved or generally recognized therapy offers an equal or greater chance of saving the subject's life[335](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.23) . The documentation must be submitted to the IRB within 5 working days after use[336](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.23) . Where there is no time for the independent physician's advance determination, a nonparticipating physician must review it in writing within 5 working days[337](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.23) . Warning letters cite certifications signed by a co-investigator instead of an uninvolved physician[986](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603195755/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075845.htm)[992](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603195755/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075845.htm) , and late or missing 5-working-day notifications, which 50.23(c) requires to the IRB and, for devices, 812.150(a)(5) requires to the sponsor[488](https://web.archive.org/web/20150613094401/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048424.htm)[489](https://web.archive.org/web/20150613094401/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048424.htm)[674](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603185414/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2007/ucm076354.htm)[675](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603185414/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2007/ucm076354.htm) .


#### Investigator obligations that tie Part 50 to the IND and IDE rules


- **Drugs and biologics.** Under 21 CFR 312.60, an investigator must obtain informed consent from each human subject to whom the drug is administered, in accordance with Part 50, except as provided in 50.22, 50.23 or 50.24[317](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.60) .
- **Devices.** Under 21 CFR 812.100, device investigators must ensure informed consent is obtained in accordance with Part 50[262](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-812.100) .


That is why drug letters usually pair Part 50 citations with 312.60, and device letters pair them with 812.100. Device letters often add 812.140(a)(3) on records of consent, or 812.150(a)(5) on reporting device use without consent.


### Practical implications for sites and sponsors


- **Version control is the first line of defense.** Check that the ICF version being signed matches the current IRB approval, at every consent and re-consent. FDA has cited both superseded versions and site edits to approved text[1044](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm148993.htm)[1073](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/informed-consent-deficiencies-in-fda-clinical?showSourceNumber=1073) .
- **Define "research procedure" conservatively.** Screening tests, randomization, run-in dosing and research blood draws done before signature all lead to findings[382](https://web.archive.org/web/20190214032318/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2013/ucm340269.htm)[459](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/mobeen-mazhar-md-660335-05312023)[1067](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/informed-consent-deficiencies-in-fda-clinical?showSourceNumber=1067) .
- **Treat optional components as separate consents.** Several recent letters (2025 to 2026) involve optional genetic, PK or tissue sampling, or drug addenda, done without the specific consent the protocol required[507](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/shirish-m-gadgeel-md-716181-09042025)[476](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/mark-s-dacey-md-722942-02022026)[501](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/mark-j-savant-mdsan-francisco-research-institute-712306-06262025) .
- **Verify who is legally authorized to sign** under applicable law, especially for minors, wards and impaired adults, and record the basis[312](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/americo-f-padilla-md-700447-03252025)[339](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604112833/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2010/ucm202614.htm)[257](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604131009/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2011/ucm244485.htm) .
- **Plan for non-English speakers** with translated full forms or a compliant 50.27(b)(2) short-form process, including a witness and an IRB-approved summary[442](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-50.27)[437](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm) .
- **Review the consent document's content against 50.25 and 50.20** before IRB submission. Remove exculpatory language, describe experimental procedures and risks accurately, and avoid statements implying FDA approval or overstating benefits[521](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/kdunn-and-associates-pa-dba-healthquilt-611864-02162021)[542](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/pratik-doshi-md-alembic-pharmaceuticals-ltd-731020-07102026)[473](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603212406/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm075951.htm)[483](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/sourav-k-mishra-md-all-india-institute-medical-sciences-724881-04292026) .
- **Keep consent records contemporaneous and original.** Subjects should date their own signatures. Consent times should be checkable against procedure times. Originals must be retained[438](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006233739/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm132595.htm)[344](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630073807/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048320.htm)[831](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603224505/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2006/ucm076082.htm) .
